articles.title: High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion
articles.snippet:
High Lander has reached $30 million in total funding as the autonomous aviation software company expands in the United States and increases its focus on defense, homeland security, and other dual-use applications.
The post High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
High Lander Reaches $30 Million In Funding To Accelerate U.S. Defense And Homeland Security Expansion
High Lander has reached $30 million in total funding as the autonomous aviation software company expands in the United States and increases its focus on defense, homeland security, and other dual-use applications.
The latest financing includes an additional strategic investment from EDGE Group along with participation from STEP, Protego, and Kinetica. High Lander plans to use the capital to expand its international operations, continue developing its autonomous aviation platforms, and strengthen its presence across national security markets.
Founded in 2018, High Lander develops software infrastructure for autonomous aviation, drone fleet operations, and low-altitude airspace management. Its technology portfolio includes Vega UTM, Orion DFM, and the newer Andromeda platform.
Vega is an Unmanned Traffic Management platform designed to coordinate uncrewed aircraft operating across complex airspace environments. Orion provides Drone Fleet Management capabilities that enable organizations to remotely manage fleets, missions, and autonomous operations.
High Lander is now extending that infrastructure into defense and homeland security through Andromeda, an AI-powered operational intelligence platform designed to create a unified view of low-altitude airspace.
Andromeda uses an open, hardware-agnostic architecture that can integrate sensors and effectors from multiple vendors under a single intelligent control layer. High Lander said the approach enables organizations to combine detection, classification, tracking, and operational response technologies while maintaining a common operational picture.
The platform is intended to help governments and other organizations distinguish authorized activity from unidentified or unauthorized aircraft as the number of drones and autonomous systems operating at low altitude increases.
The new funding will support further development of Andromeda as well as High Lander’s Vega and Orion products. The company also plans to accelerate expansion in the United States and additional international markets while pursuing strategic partnerships across autonomous systems, aerospace, defense technology, and homeland security.
EDGE Group’s latest investment builds on an existing strategic relationship with High Lander. The company said participation from STEP, Protego, and Kinetica also expands its network within the U.S. autonomous systems market and the broader global defense technology ecosystem.
High Lander is positioning its software as an infrastructure layer connecting autonomous aircraft, aviation management, and security systems. As drone adoption expands across commercial and government markets, the company sees increasing demand for software capable of coordinating both routine autonomous operations and security responses within increasingly crowded low-altitude airspace.

Over the past several years, we have built the technological infrastructure that enables countries and organizations to manage a world in which autonomous systems are becoming an integral part of the airspace. articles.title: National Math Stars Receives $30 Million NSF Grant
articles.snippet:
National Math Stars received a $30 million grant from the National Science Foundation to expand its programs identifying and supporting mathematically exceptional young students.
The post National Math Stars Receives $30 Million NSF Grant appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
National Math Stars Receives $30 Million NSF Grant
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
National Math Stars Receives $30 Million NSF Grant
National Math Stars received a $30 million grant from the National Science Foundation to expand its programs identifying and supporting mathematically exceptional young students.
The funding comes from the NSF Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships and will be deployed over four years.
National Math Stars plans to expand its programs from 10 states to areas representing approximately 75% of the U.S. population.
Founded in 2023, the nonprofit identifies young students with advanced mathematical ability and provides resources designed to support their development over multiple years.
In 2026, National Math Stars worked with three state education agencies and nearly 1,000 school districts to screen second- and third-grade students.
More than 20,000 children scoring in the top 2% on existing standardized mathematics assessments received recognition through the Math Awards Program.
Students can subsequently apply to the organization’s Stars Program.
The long-term program provides advanced coursework, enrichment opportunities, advising, community, and financial assistance based on need.
More than 900 students are currently participating as National Math Stars.
With the new NSF funding, the organization plans to screen more than 1.8 million second-, third-, and fourth-grade students annually.
By 2030, NMS expects to support more than 4,100 students through its 10-year programs and aims to reach 12,000 students annually by 2035.
The grant will also fund development and testing of an AI-assisted digital platform designed to provide personalized academic guidance at a lower cost per student.
KEY QUOTES:
“We aim to find extraordinary young mathematicians in every part of the country and foster their talents. These children are a future generation of researchers, inventors, and founders, but early support is essential to make those futures possible.”
Ilana Walder-Biesanz, Founder and CEO of National Math Stars
“This will ensure that talented children can develop their abilities regardless of where they live or their family’s income.”
Erwin Gianchandani, NSF Assistant Director for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships

articles.title: Vates Raises €30 Million To Accelerate North American Growth And Open-Source Virtualization Platform
articles.snippet:
Vates has raised €30 million, approximately $33.6 million, in funding led by IRIS's Growth fund and Bpifrance through its Large Venture fund, giving the open-source virtualization company new capital to accelerate technology development, expand its enterprise go-to-market organization and scale internationally.
The post Vates Raises €30 Million To Accelerate North American Growth And Open-Source Virtualization Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Vates Raises €30 Million To Accelerate North American Growth And Open-Source Virtualization Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Vates Raises €30 Million To Accelerate North American Growth And Open-Source Virtualization Platform
Vates has raised €30 million, approximately $33.6 million, in funding led by IRIS’s Growth fund and Bpifrance through its Large Venture fund, giving the open-source virtualization company new capital to accelerate technology development, expand its enterprise go-to-market organization and scale internationally.
The financing marks Vates’ first major outside funding after nearly a decade of self-funded growth.
Vates develops XCP-ng, an open-source virtualization platform, and the Vates Virtualization Management Stack, or Vates VMS. The company now serves more than 1,000 customers across approximately 100 countries.
North America already accounts for close to 50% of Vates’ business, with customers including Harman, AMD and North Carolina State University.
About 90% of the company’s revenue is generated outside France.
Vates grew more than 65% in 2025 and was recently included for the first time in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Server Virtualization Platforms.
The company said the new financing is therefore intended to accelerate an established North American business rather than fund an initial entry into the market.
Vates plans to invest significantly in the next generation of its virtualization platform, particularly across performance, storage, security, automation and management of large-scale virtualization environments.
Those investments will also address changing infrastructure requirements associated with artificial intelligence and other emerging workloads.
The company will also expand its enterprise sales, marketing and customer-facing resources, with North America representing a major focus.
Vates intends to increase its presence among large enterprises, public-sector organizations and service providers while investing further in channel partnerships and technology alliances.
Another portion of the funding will be directed toward expanding Vates’ global partner ecosystem, including distributors, systems integrators, service providers and technology partners.
The company sees those relationships as increasingly important as customers undertake larger infrastructure transformation and migration programs.
The investment comes during a period of significant change in the virtualization market.
Broadcom’s acquisition of VMware has prompted many organizations to reconsider their virtualization strategies as they evaluate licensing structures, vendor concentration, infrastructure complexity and long-term platform flexibility.
Vates is positioning its open-source architecture as an alternative for enterprises seeking greater control over their virtualization environments.
Its platform combines open-source technology with enterprise support, professional services and operational capabilities intended for business-critical workloads.
The company emphasizes interoperability, portability and transparency as ways for customers to reduce dependence on a single infrastructure vendor while retaining flexibility as their technology strategies change.
Vates said open source will remain central to its operating model following the new investment.
The company’s co-founders will remain majority shareholders after the transaction, preserving their control of the business.

articles.title: Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform
articles.snippet:
Arboretum LifeSciences has launched with $30 million in Series A funding to expand access to genetic testing for common diseases and build a molecular information platform supporting precision medicine and genomically stratified clinical trials. The financing was led by F-Prime, GV, .406 Ventures, Hims & Hers, Amgen and other healthcare investors.
The post Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Arboretum Raises $30 Million Series A And Launches Precision Medicine Platform
Arboretum LifeSciences has launched with $30 million in Series A funding to expand access to genetic testing for common diseases and build a molecular information platform supporting precision medicine and genomically stratified clinical trials. The financing was led by F-Prime, GV, .406 Ventures, Hims & Hers, Amgen and other healthcare investors.
Arboretum was founded by leaders from the Broad Institute’s Data Sciences Platform and combines artificial intelligence, genomic testing and clinical data.
The company is initially focused on common conditions such as cardiovascular, metabolic and autoimmune diseases, areas where precision medicine has advanced more slowly than in oncology and rare disease.
For healthcare systems, Arboretum provides clinical genetic testing and access to a collaborative research network.
The model is intended to identify patients who may be at risk for preventable diseases, return actionable genomic findings and build molecular datasets capable of supporting research and precision clinical trials.
For biopharmaceutical companies, Arboretum plans to provide genomically stratified clinical development capabilities, patient matching and datasets that can support target discovery, trial design and commercialization.
The company has established healthcare partnerships with Advocate Health, Geisinger, Providence Healthcare and Cardiovascular Associates of America.
At Advocate Health, its testing will support the organization’s cardiogenetics service line and Advocate CV Genetics Registry.
At Geisinger, Arboretum will provide clinical genetic testing supporting MyCode-Connect, while its work with Providence will integrate testing and research infrastructure with existing registries.
Cardiovascular Associates of America will use point-of-care genetic testing across its specialty practice network.
KEY QUOTES:
“We started Arboretum to solve one of the biggest problems in therapeutics development: identifying genetically-defined populations that will have outsized benefit from common disease therapies. Twenty years ago, the field of oncology opted to leverage molecular information to find therapies that would treat smaller populations but have more transformative outcomes than general chemotoxic agents. This is a moment in time to make a similar bet on diseases like coronary artery disease, diabetes, and neurodegeneration. The goal of Arboretum is to build the scientific and operational infrastructure that turns that thesis into better therapies.”
Anthony Philippakis, M.D., Ph.D., Co-Founder and CEO of Arboretum and General Partner at GV
“Our focus is on building a durable and actionable research network that places patients at the center. Improving patient care is our utmost goal. By engaging patients in research, and designing clinical trials around the biological signal of each patient rather than population averages, we give patients better therapeutic options and create the clinical evidence needed for tomorrow’s diagnostics and therapeutics.”
Clare Bernard, Ph.D., President of Arboretum

articles.title: Trustar Bankshares Raises $28.1 Million To Support Growth And Forbright Branch Acquisition
articles.snippet:
Trustar Bankshares has entered into an agreement for a $28.1 million private placement led by JCSD Mclean Investors and certain Trustar directors. The financing is intended to provide additional capital as Trustar Bank prepares to complete its previously announced acquisition of certain branches and related assets from Forbright Bank.
The post Trustar Bankshares Raises $28.1 Million To Support Growth And Forbright Branch Acquisition appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Trustar Bankshares Raises $28.1 Million To Support Growth And Forbright Branch Acquisition
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Trustar Bankshares Raises $28.1 Million To Support Growth And Forbright Branch Acquisition
Trustar Bankshares has entered into an agreement for a $28.1 million private placement led by JCSD Mclean Investors and certain Trustar directors. The financing is intended to provide additional capital as Trustar Bank prepares to complete its previously announced acquisition of certain branches and related assets from Forbright Bank.
Trustar will sell $28.1 million of common stock and, to the extent JCSD’s investment would exceed 9.9% voting ownership, newly created non-voting convertible preferred stock.
The company expects to issue 1,372,700 common shares and 877,300 shares of Convertible, Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A.
Both securities are priced at $12.50 per share.
The private placement is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close concurrently with Trustar Bank’s Forbright branch acquisition.
That transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and was expected to close as early as the fourth quarter of 2026.
Trustar plans to use proceeds for general corporate purposes, including supporting the capital of Trustar Bank after completion of the branch acquisition.
Under the agreement, Trustar will register the common stock held by JCSD, including common shares issued following conversion of the preferred shares, for resale within two years of closing.
Support: Brean Capital provided a fairness opinion to Trustar’s Board of Directors. Troutman Pepper Locke served as legal counsel to Trustar, while Gunster represented JCSD.
KEY QUOTES:
“This investment is an exciting milestone for Trustar and reflects the continued strength and momentum of our franchise. We are delighted by the confidence JCSD and our participating directors have shown in Trustar, our team, and our growth strategy. Together with our previously announced branch acquisition, this additional capital positions us well to continue expanding our franchise, serving our clients and communities, and building long-term value for our shareholders.”
Shaza Andersen, Chief Executive Officer of Trustar Bankshares and Trustar Bank

articles.title: XIVER Secures €28 Million Senior Debt Financing From ABN AMRO For €55 Million Investment Program
articles.snippet:
ABN AMRO is providing €28 million in senior debt financing to Dutch semiconductor company XIVER as part of a €55 million investment program designed to expand manufacturing capacity and technological capabilities.
The post XIVER Secures €28 Million Senior Debt Financing From ABN AMRO For €55 Million Investment Program appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
XIVER Secures €28 Million Senior Debt Financing From ABN AMRO For €55 Million Investment Program
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
XIVER Secures €28 Million Senior Debt Financing From ABN AMRO For €55 Million Investment Program
ABN AMRO is providing €28 million in senior debt financing to Dutch semiconductor company XIVER as part of a €55 million investment program designed to expand manufacturing capacity and technological capabilities.
Eindhoven-based XIVER develops and manufactures integrated photonic chips, infrared sensor technologies, medical imaging technologies and advanced thin-film products.
The investment program will support upgrades to XIVER’s manufacturing facilities and equipment base.
One of the largest investments is the acquisition of an ASML deep ultraviolet lithography system, which the company expects to strengthen its production capacity and technical capabilities.
XIVER was carved out of Philips at the High Tech Campus Eindhoven and acquired by Dutch investors in early 2025.
Since the transaction, the company has expanded its operations and built relationships with a growing group of international customers.
The new production capacity is intended to meet increasing demand for semiconductor and photonics technologies driven by markets including artificial intelligence, defense and other strategic technology applications.
ABN AMRO said the financing aligns with its strategy of supporting European companies operating in strategically important sectors including technology, energy, defense and mobility.
KEY QUOTES:
“As global competition for critical technologies intensifies, Europe must continue to invest in innovative semiconductor and photonics companies that strengthen its technological capabilities and economic resilience. At ABN AMRO, supporting these strategic sectors is a key part of our ambition to contribute to Europe’s technological resilience and long-term economic strength. We are proud to support XIVER’s growth journey and contribute to the scaling of a Dutch technology company that is becoming an increasingly important player in the global semiconductor ecosystem.”
Hans Jansen, Senior Corporate Banker at ABN AMRO
“I am extremely proud of what our team has achieved in such a short period of time. With the support of our investors and ABN AMRO, we can now substantially scale our production capacity to meet the rapidly growing production requirements of our global customer base. At the same time, these investments further strengthen our technological and industrial position and represent an important next step towards establishing XIVER in a strategically controlling position within the global semiconductor value chain.”
Wil van de Wiel, CEO of XIVER
“We can now accelerate the further expansion of our position within the European semiconductor and photonics ecosystem. Demand for our products and services is being driven by major global developments in AI, defence and the semiconductor industry as a whole. XIVER has the technology, infrastructure and industrialisation expertise required to play an increasingly important role in these rapidly growing markets.”
Cees Meeuwis, Founder and Lead Investor of XIVER

articles.title: 6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion
articles.snippet:
6K Additive has executed a final $27.4 million secured loan agreement with the Export-Import Bank of the United States to expand domestic manufacturing capacity for critical materials used in aerospace, defense, space, energy and advanced industrial applications.
The post 6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
6K Additive Secures $27.4 Million EXIM Loan For U.S. Manufacturing Expansion
6K Additive has executed a final $27.4 million secured loan agreement with the Export-Import Bank of the United States to expand domestic manufacturing capacity for critical materials used in aerospace, defense, space, energy and advanced industrial applications.
The six-year facility is available for drawdown through June 30, 2028.
The financing includes an initial 12-month interest-only period followed by amortizing principal payments during the remaining five years.
The loan will carry a fixed Commercial Interest Reference Rate determined five business days before the first disbursement. The published rate cited in the announcement was 5.38%.
Up to $25.2 million of the facility will finance eligible project costs, while up to $2.2 million will finance an 8.9% EXIM exposure fee on disbursements.
6K estimated an all-in annual borrowing cost of approximately 6.86% based on then-current published rates. The facility also includes a 0.5% annual commitment fee on undrawn and uncanceled commitments during the drawdown period.
Proceeds are immediately available to reimburse 6K for equipment and infrastructure purchases related to expansion of its Burgettstown, Pennsylvania, manufacturing facility.
The expansion includes four new buildings and additional manufacturing equipment intended to increase production of nickel, titanium, tungsten, C-103 and other advanced metal powders.
The loan was approved through EXIM’s Make More in America Initiative in coordination with the U.S. Department of War’s Defense Production Act Title III initiative.
6K said the financing was initially approved by EXIM’s board in December 2025, subject to completion of final loan documentation.
KEY QUOTES:
“Finalizing this agreement with EXIM marks an important milestone for 6K Additive and reinforces the strategic importance of expanding domestic production of the critical materials essential to America’s defense and advanced manufacturing industries. This investment directly supports the Make More in America Initiative and provides 6K Additive with the funding required to execute our planned capacity expansion while preserving our existing capital to support continued growth. We greatly appreciate EXIM Chairman John Jovanovic’s leadership and support in bringing this agreement to completion.”
Frank Roberts, CEO of 6K Additive
